ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Internal Medicine
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Dysuria and a clear discharge from his penis for the past three days

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns with complaints similar to prior encounters in January and July 2020. He reports dysuria and a clear discharge from his penis for the past three days. He reports no fever, rash, or joint pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Chlamydia trachomatis infection (Cervicitis) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Chlamydia trachomatis urethritis (diagnosed 2020-07-15)

MEDICATIONS:
He takes no medications

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with essential hypertension (diagnosed age 45)
- Paternal grandfather with hyperlipidemia
- Mother with hypothyroidism
- No family history of bleeding disorders or malignancy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
He is sexually active with multiple partners and inconsistently uses condoms. His last sexual encounter was two weeks ago.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, there is no penile lesion or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

LABORATORY DATA:
Urinalysis is unremarkable. Nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) of the urethral discharge is positive for Chlamydia trachomatis.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Internal Medicine
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Burning sensation during urination and a mucopurulent discharge from his penis for three days

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He reports having unprotected sexual intercourse with a new partner two weeks prior. He denies any recent travel, sick contacts, or similar symptoms in the past.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
His medical history is unremarkable

MEDICATIONS:
He takes no medications.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with essential hypertension (diagnosed age 45)
- Paternal grandfather with hyperlipidemia
- Mother with hypothyroidism
- No family history of bleeding disorders or malignancy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional social use (2-3 drinks on weekends). Occupation: Graduate student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, there is no rash, lymphadenopathy, or joint swelling. Genital examination reveals a clear mucopurulent discharge from the urethra. No lesions or ulcers are noted on the penis.

LABORATORY DATA:
A urine sample is collected, and the following tests are performed:

- Urinalysis: Normal
- Urine Gram stain: No organisms seen
- Urine culture: No growth
- Nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) for Neisseria gonorrhoeae: Negative

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-07-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Urgent Care
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
4-day history of dysuria and watery urethral discharge

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns for genitourinary complaints six months after his prior presentation to Internal Medicine for similar symptoms. He denies fever, testicular pain, or any genital ulcers. He reports recent unprotected sexual intercourse with two new female partners within the past month. He is concerned about sexually transmitted infections and is awaiting further testing.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Chlamydia trachomatis infection (Cervicitis) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with essential hypertension (diagnosed age 45)
- Paternal grandfather with hyperlipidemia
- Mother with hypothyroidism
- No family history of bleeding disorders or malignancy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional social use (2-3 drinks on weekends). Occupation: Graduate student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical exam, the urethral meatus is erythematous with a mucopurulent discharge. No inguinal lymphadenopathy or scrotal tenderness is noted.

LABORATORY DATA:
Urinalysis shows pyuria. Gram stain of the urethral discharge reveals numerous neutrophils but no visible organisms.

PLAN:
The clinician orders nucleic acid amplification testing to confirm the diagnosis. Empiric treatment is planned.
